ai.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro pricing note updated for 08/16 repricing
ai.summary: Comments in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` documenting `DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL` and `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID` were rewritten to reflect DeepSeek's 16:00 UTC 2026-08-16 family repricing that split the model into off-peak and peak pricing tiers (double at peak), removing the previous single-tier note. The Pro default (`DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID`) was left unchanged, but its docblock now records that the repricing flipped Pro from cheaper-than-Luna to dearer-than-Luna on cache reads, and notes the cost argument behind Pro being the browser default no longer holds and should be revisited. `FREEBUFF_WEB_DEEMPHASIZED_MODEL_IDS` was left empty and the docblock explicitly states muting is a product-steering decision the repricing alone should not silently overturn.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, the comment above `DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL` (around line 605) was edited to document DeepSeek's 16:00 UTC 2026-08-16 repricing that split the Pro family into off-peak ($0.66 in / $0.87 cache read / $1.98 out per M) and peak (exactly double) tiers, replacing the prior single-tier pricing note. The comment above `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID` (around line 1279) was likewise updated to state that the repricing inverted the cache-read cost comparison versus GPT-5.6 Luna and to leave the default on Pro while flagging the cost half of the argument as no longer holding.

ai.title: Spend ceiling docs clarify 2x hard cap and live session behavior
ai.summary: The docblock and rationale comments in `common/src/constants/freebuff-spend-ceilings.ts` now describe the 1x fresh-admission gate alongside the separate 2x `FREEBUFF_SPEND_CEILING_HARD_MULTIPLIER` cut on live reclaims and new prompts for restricted cohorts. No numeric ceilings changed: `FREEBUFF_RESTRICTED_DAILY_SPEND_USD` stays at $0.50 and `FREEBUFF_SPEND_CEILING_HARD_MULTIPLIER` stays at 2, so the gating logic is identical and only the human-facing justification was rewritten. The rewrite makes explicit that `region`, `elevated_country` and `trust_level` ceilings never trigger the hard live cut because their overshoot is proportionally small.
ai.evidence: Reworked the file-level docblock and the `FREEBUFF_SPEND_CEILING_HARD_MULTIPLIER` comment in `common/src/constants/freebuff-spend-ceilings.ts` to describe the fresh-admission gate plus the 2x hard cap, and adjusted `FREEBUFF_RESTRICTED_NOTICE_REASONS` wording around `unverified_egress`; numeric constants such as `FREEBUFF_RESTRICTED_DAILY_SPEND_USD = 0.5` and `FREEBUFF_SPEND_CEILING_HARD_MULTIPLIER = 2` are unchanged.

facts: DeepSeek's peak pricing windows, the one definition, shared by the billing code that prices a request and the product code that tells a user why their allowance is smaller right now.
Peak hours, from api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing (read 2026-08-16): "Peak hours are 01:00 - 04:00 and 06:00 - 10:00 UTC (all other hours are off-peak)." Every rate doubles inside them.
When the CURRENT window ends, the instant the rate changes.

This is what a user is actually asking when they hit a reduced cap: not "when is peak" but "when do I get my normal allowance back". Returns the next boundary in either direction, so it also answers "when does the cheap period end" for an off-peak caller.
Unreachable while both windows exist; a defined answer beats a throw on a path that only ever renders a help string.

entries.summary: New files: `common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts`.

ai.title: DeepSeek peak-hours spend ceiling and notice added
ai.summary: A new `common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts` defines DeepSeek's peak windows (UTC 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00, half-open) with `isDeepSeekPeakHour`, `nextDeepSeekWindowBoundary`, and `formatDeepSeekPeakWindowsLocal`. `resolveFreebuffSpendCeiling` now takes an optional `at` and `peakMultiplier`; when both are set and the instant falls in a peak window, it halves the winning ceiling's `usd` and returns it under a new `peak` field carrying `baseUsd`, multiplier, and an `endsAt` boundary. The reduced ceiling also gets a dedicated `FREEBUFF_PEAK_LIMIT_NOTICE` refusal string and a matching `spend_limited` .peak shape that the CLI can use to say the limit returns in hours rather than at midnight Pacific.
ai.evidence: New `common/src/constants/freebuff-peak-hours.ts` exports `DEEPSEEK_PEAK_HOUR_RANGES_UTC` ([1,4],[6,10]), `isDeepSeekPeakHour`, `nextDeepSeekWindowBoundary`, `formatDeepSeekPeakWindowsLocal`; `common/src/constants/freebuff-spend-ceilings.ts` imports them, adds `FreebuffSpendCeilingPeak`/`peak` field, and `resolvePeakReduction` now halves `winner.usd` via `peakMultiplier` when `isDeepSeekPeakHour(at)`; `/api/v1/freebuff/session` now omits `windowHours`.
ai.unknowns: The commit does not show the CLI or server call site that passes `at`/`peakMultiplier`, so the customer-facing rollout path is not in the diff.
